title: Why Did Carlos Alcaraz Smile After Losing at 3:34 in the Morning?
summary:
Imagine playing a tennis match that ends at 3:34 in the morning. You've been running and hitting for almost four and a half hours. You lose. Would you smile?

Carlos Alcaraz did. He's one of the best tennis players in the world, with seven Grand Slam titles. But at the US Open, he lost a long, tough match to Ben Shelton. It was the latest finish in the tournament's history.

As Alcaraz walked through the tunnel, cameras caught him grinning from ear to ear. Why? Because he had been injured for more than five months. A wrist injury hurt every day. He missed the French Open and Wimbledon. He didn't even know if he could play in New York until a week before.

"I suffered, but I enjoyed," he said. "That's why I smiled when I walked out of the court because I missed that feeling."

Alcaraz also thinks matches shouldn't end so late. "I think it's too much," he said. He wants a rule that says no match can finish after 11 p.m.

Next, he's playing for Team Europe in the Laver Cup in London. "When you have your team-mates, the best in the world, by your side, it's a weird feeling but it's beautiful," he said.
why_it_matters: It shows that losing is not the same as failing — sometimes being able to play at all is already the win, and that is something everyone can remember when things go badly at school or in sports.

background_read: Carlos Alcaraz (one of the best tennis players in the world, from Spain) has won several of the sport's biggest prizes.
The four biggest tennis tournaments are called the Grand Slams: the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open, which is played in New York.
Tennis has had very late finishes before — at Wimbledon in 2010, two players finished a match that lasted more than 11 hours over three days.
Many players and fans say finishing at 3 o'clock in the morning is bad for the players and hard for the fans who have to travel home.
Article_Structure: WHO: Carlos Alcaraz, a top tennis player, and Ben Shelton, the player who beat him.
WHAT: Alcaraz lost a match that lasted almost four and a half hours and ended at 3:34 in the morning — the latest finish in US Open history.
WHERE: At the US Open in New York; his next competition is the Laver Cup in London.
WHY: He smiled because he had missed playing for more than five months with a wrist injury, so he was happy just to be back on court.

perspectives.description: They are proud that he came back after five months of injury and could still enjoy the game, even in a loss.
They agree with Alcaraz that matches should not run past 11 p.m., because players need sleep and fans have to get home safely.
Some people say night matches are exciting because the crowds are loud and the stadiums are full, but the schedule is clearly hard on everyone.
